**Answer: ATE ≈ -7.36 days** (negative, so the medication shortens recovery time in this estimate).

I used 1-nearest-neighbour matching with replacement, since the question gives no k. Covariates were z-scored (sex, age, severity), matching used Euclidean distance, and the bias correction is the Abadie–Imbens adjustment, with outcome regressions fit separately within each treatment group.

Results by k:

| k | Uncorrected ATE | Bias-corrected ATE |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | -0.99 | **-7.36** |
| 2 | -0.67 | -7.43 |
| 3 | -0.48 | -7.47 |
| 5 | -0.22 | -7.54 |
| 10 | +0.13 | -7.64 |

The bias correction is large relative to the raw estimate, because matches are imperfect and the regression slopes are steep (for example, severity has a coefficient of about 60 days per unit in the control regression). The corrected estimate is fairly stable across k, which is reassuring. The uncorrected estimate is sensitive to k and changes sign, so it is not a reliable basis for an answer.

ANSWER: -7.36
